cards.answer: Kassadin is an AP assassin and mage who blinks into enemies to deal magic damage. Repeated Riftwalks increase his damage and mana cost.
cards.counterplay: Keep your distance and avoid clustering around his arrival point.

cards.answer: Void Stone reduces the magic damage Kassadin takes and lets him ignore unit collision.
cards.counterplay: Avoid relying on magic damage alone, and do not rely on minions to obstruct his movement.

cards.answer: Null Sphere targets an enemy, deals magic damage, and interrupts ongoing channels. Kassadin also gains a brief shield that absorbs magic damage.
cards.counterplay: Be cautious about channeling within his reach, and delay magic damage trades while his shield is active.

cards.answer: Nether Blade passively adds magic damage to Kassadin's basic attacks. Its active empowers his next basic attack with extra range and increased bonus magic damage, restoring more mana against champions. It also resets his basic attack timer.
cards.counterplay: Keep out of melee reach to limit his empowered attacks and mana recovery.

cards.answer: Force Pulse deals magic damage and briefly slows enemies in a cone. Ability casts by Kassadin or nearby champions reduce its remaining cooldown.
cards.counterplay: Spread out and be ready for another cone during spell-heavy fights.

citations.quote: Active: Kassadin emits a pulse of void energy in a cone in the target direction that deals magic damage to enemies and briefly slows them.

facts.claim: Force Pulse deals magic damage and briefly slows enemies in a cone.

facts.claim: Ability casts by Kassadin or nearby champions reduce its remaining cooldown.

cards.priority_reason: Its area slow and accelerated availability matter in fights with frequent casts.

cards.answer: Riftwalk blinks Kassadin toward a location and deals magic damage to nearby enemies on arrival. Repeated casts build temporary stacks that increase its damage and mana cost. Grounding disables Riftwalk.
cards.counterplay: Avoid clustering near his arrival point; use grounding to restrict his mobility and respect the damage from repeated casts.
